$comment: UV tile discard layout. Every vertex carries a second UV set (index 1, `uvChannel`) whose only job is to say which toggle group the face belongs to: all of a group's UVs sit inside one whole-number tile, and lilToon's UDIM Discard drops the tiles a toggle switches off. Tile (0,0) is never discarded. Because this is one float per tile on the material rather than one renderer per toggle, every group can live in the same mesh and material slot. `shown` is the state with nothing animating it. Android and iOS builds cannot switch tiles: they cut the hidden ones out of the mesh and show the rest for good, within a limit of 15,000 triangles, so a tile with `mobile` false is cut from those builds as well although it rests shown. `hides` names the body zones a garment fully covers, so wearing it discards the skin underneath instead of fighting it for depth. `toggle` gives a tile a synced switch: the tile is shown while `parameter` has the value `when` (true unless stated), every parameter in `needs` is on and every one in `unless` is off. A `label` puts the parameter in the Outfit menu. Two tiles that share a parameter with opposite `when` are alternatives, so the short and the long hair are one switch; `unless` makes the shorts give way to the skirt, and `needs` keeps the vest for when the sweater it is fitted to is worn. `rests` gives the value a parameter rests at where the tile's own resting state does not say: the shorts rest hidden because the skirt is worn over them, and their switch rests on, so that taking the skirt off shows them.

tiles.note: Head, hands, anything no toggle may hide.
